The interdisciplinary team at Emory University and Georgia Tech is recruiting a Postdoctoral Fellow in Multimodal Sensing, Mobile AI, and Digital Health.

We are looking for a researcher interested in developing human-centered AI and ubiquitous computing technologies for real-world healthcare, with a particular focus on Parkinson’s disease and human movement assessment.

Our team brings together researchers across Biomedical Informatics, Biomedical Engineering, Neurology, Electrical and Computer Engineering, and Machine Learning. The fellow will work with Hyeok Kwon (PI,

) and closely collaborate with engineering researchers and movement-disorders clinicians.

Research directions include:

• Multimodal sensing and human activity recognition using video, mobile, wearable, and clinical data
• Computer vision and machine learning for quantitative assessment of human movement
• Mobile, edge, and cloud AI for real-world clinical environments
• Clinician-in-the-loop and continual learning systems that adapt to users and changing clinical conditions
• Design and evaluation of AI systems through real-world deployment in Emory Movement Disorders clinics

The position offers a unique opportunity to develop new computational methods while working directly with clinicians, patients, multimodal clinical data, and real-world AI deployments.

We particularly welcome candidates with backgrounds in UbiComp, HCI, mobile/wearable sensing, human activity recognition, multimodal learning, computer vision, mobile/edge computing, or digital health.

The position is supported by a five-year NIH R01-funded study. (

Interested candidates are also welcome to contact Hyeok Kwon at hyeokhyen.kwon@emory.edu or hyeokhyen.kwon@gatech.edu.

Please feel free to forward this announcement to potentially interested candidates.
